Net revenue was $71,965 million in fiscal 2019 and $79,024 million in fiscal 2021. It then fell to $63,054 million in fiscal 2022 and $54,228 million in fiscal 2023. The documents give no fiscal 2020 figure. Total change from fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2023: $54,228M - $71,965M = -$17,737 million, or -$17,737M / $71,965M = about -24.6%. That is a decline, not growth. Revenue did grow from fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2021: $79,024M - $71,965M = $7,059 million, or $7,059M / $71,965M = about 9.8%. That growth was more than reversed in fiscal 2022 and 2023.

parsed.answer: No. Intel's GAAP gross margin in fiscal 2023 was 40.0% of net revenue ($21,711 million gross margin on $54,228 million revenue), not 55%. The 55% figure is close to fiscal 2021's gross margin of 55.4%, not 2023. Gross margin was 42.6% in fiscal 2022, so it fell about 2.6 percentage points in 2023 (computed: 40.0 - 42.6 = -2.6). In dollars, gross margin fell $5.2 billion, or 19%, from $26,866 million in 2022 to $21,711 million in 2023. Drivers of the $5.2 billion decline: lower product margin from lower server revenue (-$2,709 million), lower product margin from lower revenue across NEX product lines (-$1,832 million), lower product margin from lower notebook and desktop revenue (-$1,704 million), higher unit cost from increased mix of Intel 7 products (-$1,654 million), and higher excess capacity charges (-$411 million). These were partly offset by lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves (+$1,973 million), lower period charges from a decrease in product ramp costs (+$788 million), the absence of the 2022 Optane inventory impairment (+$723 million), and the absence of a 2022 patent settlement charge (+$204 million). Revenue itself fell 14% to $54.2 billion from $63.1 billion.
